chunks: And among what Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā narrated, from al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from al-Ḥasan al-Tiflīsī, who said:

I asked Abā al-Ḥasan عليه السلام about a dead person and a junub who came together, while with them there was only enough water for one of them. Which of the two should be given the ghusl? He said: “When a sunnah and an obligation come together, the obligation is begun with first.”

key_terms.بُدِئَ: precedence is given; one begins with
key_terms.جُنُبٍ: a person in the state of janabah requiring ghusl
key_terms.سُنَّةٌ: a recommended religious practice, here contrasted with an obligation
key_terms.فَرِيضَةٌ: an obligatory religious duty that takes priority
key_terms.مَيِّتٍ: a deceased person requiring ritual washing

ai.seo_question: If there is only enough water for one ghusl, should it be used for the dead person or for the junub?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about prioritization when available water is only sufficient for one ghusl. Imam Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام states that when a recommended act and an obligatory act coincide, precedence is given to the obligatory one.
